 Judgement

The Police Inspector of Jayanagar Traffic Police Station has filed the charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable U/s.279 and 304(A) of IPC, Sec.134(a and b) R/w.187 and Sec.129 R/w.194D of M.V.Act.
C.C.No.6574/2022 2.

The brief case of the prosecution is that:
On 10-04-2022 at about 9.45 p.m. within the jurisdiction of Jayanagar Traffic police station, the accused being the rider of Honda CB 350 motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-05/LE-5117 drove the same on J.P. Nagar 2nd phase, near Sampige Mara junction, 15th cross road without wearing helmet in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and
he dashed to Hero Honda Splendor motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-01-ED-7875 which was proceeding in the said road.
Due to the impact the Splendor motor cycle rider fell on road along with vehicle and sustained grievous injuries on waist and head.
Later the Splendor motor cycle rider Sri Prem Vijayan, aged about 44 years succumbed to death.
Further on the day of accident the accused did not provide medical aid to the injured nor he intimated the police about the accident.

Thereby the accused is alleged to have committed the offences punishable U/s.279 and 304(A) of IPC, Sec.134(a and b) R/w.187 and Sec.129 R/w.194D of M.V.Act.
3.

On the report of PW1, police registered FIR for offences p/u/s U/s.279 and 304(A) of IPC,
Sec.134(a and b) R/w.187 and Sec.129 R/w.194D of M.V.Act and commenced investigation.
IO prepared inquest panchnama, Seizure panchnama and spot panchnama.

4. Acting on the charge-sheet, cognizance of the offence U/s.190(1)(b) of Cr.P.C was taken and case came to be registered against accused for the offences punishable U/s.279 and 304(A) of IPC,
Sec.134(a and b) R/w.187 and Sec.129 R/w.194D of M.V.Act.
The accused appeared before the court through his learned counsel and got enlarged on bail.
Charge sheet copies were furnished to the accused and thereby provision U/s.207 of Cr.P.C. has been duly complied with.

5. Subsequently, plea came to be framed for the offences U/s.279 and 304(A) of IPC, Sec.134(a and b) R/w.187 and Sec.129 R/w.194D of M.V.Act., for which accused pleaded not guilty claimed to be tried.
6. During the course of trial, the prosecution has examined P.W.1 to 6 and got exhibited documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.

On completion of prosecution side evidence, the statement of accused U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
C.C.No.6574/2022 was recorded and the accused denied all the incriminating evidence appearing against him and did not choose to lead any defence evidence.
7. Heard arguments on both sides.

8. The points that arise for my consideration are as follows:
1.Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 10-04-2022 at about 9.45 p.m. within the jurisdiction of Jayanagar Traffic police station, the accused being the rider of Honda CB 350 motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-05/LE-5117 drove the same on J.P. Nagar 2nd phase, near Sampige Mara junction, 15th cross road in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life,
thereby the accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.279 of IPC?

2.Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place the accused being the driver of the said vehicle, drove his vehicle in the above said manner.
While so driving his vehicle he dashed to Hero Honda Splendor motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-01- ED-7875 which was proceeding in the said road.
Due to the impact the Splendor motor cycle rider fell on road along with vehicle and sustained grievous injuries on waist and head.
Later the Splendor motor cycle rider Sri Prem Vijayan, aged about 44 years succumbed to death, thereby the accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.304(A) of IPC?

sentences.text: The learned Counsel for the accused during the cross-examination of P.W.1 questioned and further argued that the death of the victim was caused due to some respiratory issues and not due to the accident.
Further it is argued that to claim compensation PW1 has deposed falsely.
This argument is further substantiated in the post mortem report as per Ex.P.11 and 12 that the cause of death is due to respiratory issues.
As per the report the death was caused due to "Respiratory failure" as a result of "Pulmonary Oedema" which can be caused in circumstances of physical fight or tension or anxiety.
This could have occurred due to road traffic accident causing the death.
Whereas the prosecution has not examined the Doctor to establish if only the accident can be the sole reason for the death of the accused.
25. Particularly P.W.4 being the eye witness has firmly deposed about the accident.
He has stated that the victim being a swiggy delivery person was riding his two- wheeler and the accused and his pillion rider without wearing helmet dashed the victim.
Not only did he cause the accident, he did not stop the motor cycle to attend to the victim.
During the course of cross examination the counsel for accused has brought multiple angles of defence.
The main defence of the accused is that the eye C.C.No.6574/2022 witness is deposing false evidence on the influence of the relatives of the victim.
During the line of cross examination is suggested that the family of the victim and PW4 had come to court together.
Another defence taken is that the location of the shop of PW4 is not very close to the spot of the accident.
It is further argued that the since the shop is located on a ring road there are multiple factors why the witness could not have seen the accident clearly.
26. PW4 being eye-witness did not depose anything about rashness or negligence of the accused.
Testimony of eye-witness is only useful to establish the presence of the vehicle and the accident at the spot.
Therefore, no evidence regarding rashness or negligence that could be established.
There is no evidence regarding how the victim was riding his two-wheeler.
The eye witness was unable to depose about the exact way the accused was driving the vehicle.
His sole testimony cannot be relied on to establish negligence.

27. In a criminal trial, the burden of establishing essential elements of crime to establish the charge sheet averments against the accused always lies on the prosecution and there is presumption of innocence in favour of the accused until the contrary is proved.
To establish the offence either under Section 279 or Section C.C.No.6574/2022 304A, the commission of a rash and negligent act has to be proved.
By considering the above said aspect it creates suspicion about the case of the prosecution regarding rash and negligent driving.
28. With respect to offences punishable U/s.134(a and b) R/w.187 of M.V.Act, it is admitted by PW4 that both the accused and his pillion rider were not wearing helmet.
Further that the accused did not stop after the accident to help or provide medical aid to the victim.
Though, eye witness was cross-examined at length by the learned Counsel for the accused, nothing worth is elicited in this regard so as to discard his testimony.
29. The counsel for accused has also cross examined the investigating officer PW6 at length.
The main contention of the accused is that CCTV footage was verified, whereas even after such verification it was not produced before the court.

The I.O during her examination in chief has Jayanagar Trps vs Darshan S on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132870794/
11 clarified that after verifying the footage of the CCTV camera it was noticed that due to lights at night the vehicle registration number was not visible.
Once the basic fact has been established it is for the accused to refute it.
The burden has then shifted to the accused to establish that the CCTV footage were available and clear.
But the accused did not choose to lead any defence evidence nor seek the court to retrieve the CCTV footage.
Hence, mere C.C.No.6574/2022 suggestion that the CCTV footage was clear and still not produced before the court does not hold ground.
30. Merely because an accident had occurred rash or negligent act cannot be presumed against the accused.
Mere speed cannot be a reason to imply rashness or negligence.
The evidence of high speed simpliciter, is not ipso facto proof of rashness or negligence.
There is no evident with regard to seed of the vehicle as well.

PW5 and 6 being the investigating officers have performed their part of duty but when clear evidence is not available to the main ingredient of rashness or negligence it does not aid the prosecution to establish the guilt of the Accused.
31. Thus, this court finds that the prosecution was unable to prove the negligence of accused which resulted in accident and injury was caused.
The accident is admitted even by the accused, thus it is not sufficient to merely prove the incident.
In the absence of clear and unambiguous evidence against accused, Accused must be given the benefit and be acquitted.
The evidence led by prosecution is deficient on the essential ingredient of rashness or negligence in driving the vehicle.
The accusations levelled against the accused remained unproved and the accusation of the prosecution is not supported by evidence to complete the chain.
Accordingly, C.C.No.6574/2022 the point No.1 and 2 under consideration are answered IN THE NEGATIVE.
32. POINT No.3:
In the instant case it is alleged that the accused has failed to provide medical aid to the injured nor he has intimated the police about the accident on the date of the accident.
And also the accused has not denied the fact that he and the pillion rider were not wearing helmet and has not rebutted the evidence regarding the said aspect.
Accordingly he has committed the offence punishable U/s.134(a and b) R/w.187 of M.V.Act.
The prosecution during the chief examination of PW4 and the cross by APP the witness has admitted that the accused did not stop after the accident had occurred.
The accused rode his two-wheeler instantly and drove away after the accident.
The accused did not choose to lead defence evidence to content this fact and has not produced any documentary evidence before the court.
Hence point No.3 and 4 are answered IN THE AFFIRMATIVE.

33. POINT No.5: In view of the above discussions and findings I proceed to pass the following C.C.No.6574/2022 ORDER Acting U/sec. 255(1) of Criminal procedure code, the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences alleged against him punishable U/sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Acting U/s.255(2) of Criminal Procedure code, the accused is hereby convicted of the offences alleged against him punishable U/s.134(a and b) R/w.187 of M.V.Act.

The accused is directed to pay fine of Rs.10,000/- for the offences punishable U/s.134(a and b)
R/w.187 of M.V.Act.
